title: Could Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both make the Patriots 53-man roster?
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Efton Chism and Kyle Williams both vying for a spot on the Patriots' 53-man roster during preseason.
The Patriots wide receiver group includes seven strong contenders, with typical NFL rosters carrying only six receivers.
Chism and Williams show promise with notable performances, complicating decisions due to potential cut risks.

title: Reports: OF George Springer interested in trade to Red Sox, team eyeing INF Xavier Edwards
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: George Springer is reportedly open to a trade to the Red Sox, who are interested under specific conditions.
Red Sox are looking at infielder Xavier Edwards from the Marlins after losing Curtis Mead to injury.
Edwards has played second base this year with a batting average of .292 and has stolen 18 bases.

title: Here’s how home, away broadcasts reacted to Jarren Duran’s on-field flare-up
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Jarren Duran's on-field flare-up sparked reactions due to his criticism toward teammate Willson Contreras and third-base coach Chad Epperson.
NESN and WEEI broadcasters criticized Duran's actions after the incident, expressing confusion and disappointment over his public outburst.
CBS Sports reports the Red Sox are open to trading Duran before the MLB trade deadline following the controversy.

title: Drake Maye on building chemistry with A.J. Brown: ‘I am not going to shy away from him.’
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown improve chemistry during Patriots' training camp, showing strong connection in recent drills.
Maye consistently targets Brown, enhancing their collaboration through frequent completions and strategic discussions.
Patriots training camp highlights include Maye's accurate throws to Brown and their effective communication strategies.

title: Drake Maye, A.J. Brown heat up and other takeaways from Day 6 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye showed precision in team drills, completing 18-of-19 throws since padded practices began on Thursday.
A.J. Brown has gained momentum, catching multiple passes from Maye during both 7-on-7 and 11-on-11 drills.
Patriots' rookie tight end Eli Raridon impressed with a touchdown catch during 7-on-7s, solidifying his backup role.

title: Massachusetts falls out of top 10 in best state rankings by U.S. News & World Report
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts ranked 11th in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best States, down from 9th in 2025.
The state ranked second in healthcare and fourth in crime and natural environment in the 2026 rankings.
Massachusetts faced challenges in fiscal stability (39th) and infrastructure (38th) impacting its overall rank.

title: Massachusetts loses two IHOP restaurants
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IHOP closed its restaurants at 16 Eliot St. in Cambridge and 790 Iyannough Road in Hyannis.
About 19 IHOP locations remain in Massachusetts after closures in Cambridge and Hyannis.
IHOP closures may be due to insufficient foot traffic or lapsed leases, part of a broader franchise model.

title: Court agrees Wu did not discriminate against North End restaurants, but may have illegally taxed them
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: A federal appeals court upheld the dismissal of a lawsuit by North End restaurants against Boston Mayor Wu's outdoor dining rules.
The lawsuit alleged racial and ethnic discrimination from outdoor dining regulations, which the appeals court rejected as unfounded.
The court allowed for a potential challenge regarding fees charged to restaurants, which could be considered an illegal tax.

title: MassDOT releases rendering of two new bridges along McGrath Highway
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MassDOT plans to replace Squires Bridge and build Somerville Avenue Extension Bridge on McGrath Highway, now McGrath Boulevard.
The Squires Bridge project spans from Third Street, Cambridge to Medford Street, Somerville, offering two traffic lanes and bike lanes.
Construction on both bridges is expected to start in 2030, with completion estimated in three to four years.
